candidates.title: R.J. Corman sues over sale of Luzerne County rail lines
candidates.excerpt: WILKES-BARRE, Pa. — R.J. Corman Railroad Co. has filed suit over the sale of rail lines in Luzerne County, Pa., according to a news report. The Wilkes-Barre Times Leader reports the company filed suit in federal court late Friday, Oct. 2, asking the court to void a decision this week selling 60 miles of active tracks and right-of-way to the Reading & Northern. Case documents do not yet appear in the federal court electronic document system. The Luzerne County Redevelopment Authority initially voted to sell the rail lines to R.J. Corman for $8.2 million, but the Luzerne County Council — which has approval rights as part of its settlement of a lawsuit against the redevelopment authority — vetoed that decision [see “Luzerne County, Pa., council rejects …,” Trains.com, Sept. 23, 2026]. The redevelopment agency and county then accepted an offer from the R&N including $7 million in cash and $3 million in infrastructure upgrades [see “Reading & Northern nears deal …,” Oct. 1, 2026]. candidates.excerpt: Sri Lanka Prime Minister Dr Harini Amarasuriya has inaugurated the Phase II expansion of APSEZ’s Colombo West International Terminal, doubling capacity from 1.6 million to 3.2 million TEUs through a total investment of US$ 750 million. The expansion advances CWIT’s ambition to handle nearly 25 percent of the Port of Colombo’s 13 million TEU target by 2028 and enables the terminal to simultaneously berth three ultra-large container vessels, strengthening Colombo’s position as a critical transshipment hub on the East-West trade route. CWIT has established a record of rapid operational growth since commencing operations in 2024, becoming the fastest terminal to handle 1 million TEUs in its inaugural year and achieving 2 million TEUs within its first 18 months of operation. candidates.title: ONE restructures regional headquarters in Asia-Pacific and Africa
candidates.excerpt: Ocean Network Express (ONE) will reorganise its regional headquarters structure in Asia-Pacific and Africa from 1 April 2027. The container carrier will establish a new Asia-Pacific Regional Headquarters in Singapore. The operation will combine its East Asia and South Asia regional functions, which are currently based in Hong Kong and Singapore. The new headquarters will oversee ONE’s business across 15 markets. Louis Tang will serve as Region Head for Asia-Pacific. ONE will also centralise the management of its East, West and Southern African markets at its Dubai Regional Headquarters. Meanwhile, its London office will continue managing Europe, the Mediterranean and North Africa. “Asia Pacific and Africa are important growth regions for ONE. Our regional headquarters sit closest to our customers and our markets, and these changes will enable us to make faster decisions and accelerate growth. candidates.title: ONE folds Hong Kong regional HQ into Singapore
candidates.excerpt: Ocean Network Express is consolidating its Asian regional management in Singapore, folding its Hong Kong-based East Asia headquarters into a new Asia Pacific operation from April 1, 2027. The Japanese containerline said the new Asia Pacific regional headquarters will combine its current East Asia operation in Hong Kong with the South Asia headquarters already based in Singapore. The enlarged unit will oversee 15 markets, with Louis Tang appointed regional head. ONE is also redrawing responsibility for Africa. Its East, West and South African businesses will move under the carrier’s Dubai regional headquarters, while London will retain responsibility for Europe, the Mediterranean and North Africa. The restructuring alters a regional setup that dates back to ONE’s creation. When NYK, MOL and K Line unveiled their merged container operation in 2017, Singapore was selected as global headquarters, with regional headquarters initially established in Hong Kong, London, Richmond and São Paulo.

The past couple of months have seen a streak of developments around wind-assisted propulsion, spanning installations, orders, vessel launches, technology approvals and new trials. MOL has launched an LNG carrier equipped with wind-assisted propulsion. Bulkers, tankers, cargo ships and gas carriers are all getting some version of the technology. candidates.excerpt: Goldman Sachs backs housebuilding lender Quantum with £500m facility Small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) lender Quantum Development Finance has secured a facility worth up to £500m from Goldman Sachs, taking its total funding from £200m to as much as £700m. The firm said the deal significantly expands its lending capacity, including the ability to offer larger loans, without changing its focus on SME housebuilders. It will also allow Quantum to fund a wider range of schemes across their lifecycle, from initial acquisition through to post-completion investment. Founded in London in 2023, Quantum provides development and bridging finance to SME housebuilders in cities and suburbs throughout England and Wales. It offers loans of up to £35m, has financed the development of 4,000 new homes to date, the firm said. candidates.excerpt: Apollo rolls out daily pricing across $850bn credit business Apollo Global Management has begun rolling out daily pricing across its $850bn (£643.7bn) credit business as the industry tries to build a more transparent private credit market. The $1tn alternatives giant launched daily pricing for investors in its investment-grade fixed income replacement products on 1 July, and said today (1 October) that it had extended this to a range of direct lending, asset-backed finance, multi-credit and opportunistic credit vehicles. Apollo chief executive Marc Rowan first set out the plan on the firm’s first-quarter earnings call in May, as private credit funds faced a surge in redemption requests from retail investors. Apollo said the move was intended to promote “greater transparency” as a wider pool of investors moves into private credit. Another strong week for industrial rail freight
candidates.excerpt: U.S. weekly rail traffic totaled 537,397 carloads and intermodal units, up 4.85 compared with the same week a year ago, the Association of American Railroads (AAR) said. Traffic for the week ending September 26 totaled 235,787 carloads, up 3% compared with the same week in 2025, while intermodal volume of 301,610 containers and trailers was 6.3% higher compared to the same week in 2025. Seven of the 10 specific carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They were led by metallic ores and metals, 9.5%; petroleum and related products, 9.4%; and chemicals, 7.2%. Shipments of farm products excluding grain and food fell by 3.3%, followed by coal, 2.1%, and motor vehicles and parts, 1.8%. Coal inventories are up 1.4 million tons since the end of 2025, while domestic consumption was down 11.4% y/y. Burglary hits moving BNSF train as container catches fire in Riverside
candidates.excerpt: A BNSF train carrying mixed freight caught fire during a burglary in Riverside, California, Thursday morning. The train was traveling from Los Angeles to Chicago, BNSF told FreightWaves. Firefighters found an open upper container burning on the moving double-stack train. Officials have not identified the items inside or reported any stolen cargo. Riverside dispatchers received the first report at 4:40 a.m. near Chicago Avenue. Early information placed the train heading west from downtown. Crews later located it moving east between Spruce and Columbia streets. Riverside Fire Department deployed 19 firefighters, four engines, one truck and a chief officer. Crews move train for access Access problems prevented crews from reaching the flames at their first location. Incident commanders directed railroad personnel to reposition the equipment farther east. candidates.title: Texmaco Rail Gets Two Orders Worth ₹131.36 Crores
candidates.excerpt: Texmaco Rail Gets Two Orders Worth ₹131.36 Crores Texmaco Rail has bagged two domestic orders worth ₹131.36 crore for wagon manufacturing and supplies. While the smaller contract from TCI must be delivered within 16 weeks, the larger order from its joint venture partner Touax Texmaco is slated for completion by May 2027. Market snapshot: Texmaco Rail & Engineering Limited has secured two separate domestic orders collectively valued at ₹131.36 crore. The mandate comprises a ₹24.48 crore contract from Transport Corporation of India Limited and a ₹106.88 crore related-party contract from Touax Texmaco Railcar Leasing Private Limited. Data Snapshot - Texmaco Rail secured two domestic orders totaling ₹131.36 crore. - The order from Touax Texmaco Railcar Leasing is valued at ₹106.88 crore for the supply of 4 BFNS rakes and 4 brake vans. - The contract from Transport Corporation of India is valued at ₹24.48 crore for the supply of 1 ACT wagon rake and 1 brake van.
